name: Datadog
description: Developer/infra platform: cloud monitoring and observability (metrics, logs, traces, monitors, dashboards) with a broad REST API.
access_notes: Self-serve signup with a free trial and a limited free plan; API keys and application keys are generated by any user from Organization Settings. OAuth2 clients are for building published integrations via the developer platform.
mcp_notes: Official remote Datadog MCP Server (docs.datadoghq.com/mcp_server) covering APM, logs, metrics, monitors, dashboards, security signals; auth via OAuth 2.0, PAT/SAT, or API+app key headers. Composio DATADOG toolkit exists (65 tools, own-credentials auth).
uncertainty_notes: Free plan exists (limited hosts) but the exact current free-plan API entitlements were not verified on the pricing page, so access is recorded as self_serve_trial. OAuth2 is documented for third-party integrations but creating published OAuth clients goes through Datadog's developer/integration platform; day-to-day API use is API key + application key.

evidence.note: 'All requests to Datadog's API must be authenticated' - API key (DD-API-KEY) for writes, plus application key (DD-APPLICATION-KEY) for reads; HTTP REST API.
API and application keys are self-managed in Organization Settings by account users.
Datadog uses the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework to let third-party applications access Datadog resources on behalf of users, with granular scopes.
Webhooks integration: 'Alert your services when a metric alert is triggered' - outbound POST with JSON payload from monitors/events.
Official 'Datadog MCP Server' docs: remote MCP bridging observability data to AI agents; setup supports OAuth 2.0, PAT/SAT, or API+application key headers.
Composio toolkit catalog lists Datadog (slug DATADOG, 65 tools, OAUTH2/API_KEY/BEARER_TOKEN, no managed app).
